answer: Lantern Consensus Cipher enforces cross-epoch consistency by requiring persistent behavior patterns across time. An attacker must maintain a coherent identity narrative spanning multiple epochs, paying a pulse of reputation cost with each inconsistency. This mechanism makes sybil attacks prohibitively expensive as they cannot fabricate the long-term behavioral coherence required. The cipher's lantern pulse reveals fragmented identities, exposing those who fail the consistency rule through their inability to sustain a unified behavioral signature over time.
